title: Design and Implementation of Harm Reduction Policies in Germany
summary:
Harm reduction services in Germany aim to reduce health and social harms related to psychoactive substance use. This study seeks to understand how harm reduction strategies are designed, implemented, and adapted across different regions in Germany, and which factors stakeholders believe contribute to their effectiveness.

We will conduct one semi structured interview lasting about 60 to 90 minutes with 12 to 20 adults who are involved in harm reduction strategy design, implementation, or evaluation in Germany. Participation is voluntary. Audio recording is optional. Participants are also asked to provide general, aggregated information at the level of their organization, such as patterns of service utilization and characteristics of the populations they serve. No individual client or patient data are collected. Findings will be used to develop recommendations to strengthen harm reduction strategies in Germany and inform harm reduction efforts in the United States.
conditions: Health and social harms related to psychoactive substance use, including overdose risk and infectious disease risks (for example HIV and hepatitis C), and the implementation of harm reduction strategies in Germany.

interventions.name: Stakeholders in Germany involved in harm reduction strategy design, implementation, or evaluation, participation in one semi structured interview plus provision of aggregated facility level context data.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults only (age 18 years or older)

Policy makers, public health professionals, or researchers directly involved in the development, implementation, evaluation, or practical delivery of harm reduction strategies and services in Germany

Sufficient English proficiency to participate in an interview conducted in English

Willingness to provide informed consent and participate in a 60 to 90 minute interview
Exclusion criteria:
Under 18 years of age

No direct professional experience with harm reduction strategies or services

Insufficient English proficiency to meaningfully participate in the interview

Unwilling or unable to provide informed consent
